text:
support_alex: FYI customer ACME-Sec reports a ~1h gap in audit exports overnight (02:00-03:00 UTC). Splunk shows no events for that window. Can we triage? :eyes:
eng_raj: Do we know if they used the tenant filter or a time-range query? first hunch is timestamp parsing/ingest.
support_alex: They queried the export manifest for start=2026-03-15T02:00:00Z end=2026-03-15T03:00:00Z and got an empty file list. I asked them to share the manifest but they sent this small excerpt — looks like batches exist around the gap but not in the expected bucket prefix:
```json
{"files": ["s3://redwood-audit-exports/acme/2026-03-15/01/part-0001.gz","s3://redwood-audit-exports/acme/2026-03-15/03/part-0003.gz"]}
```
sre_maya: interesting — so 02h doesn't have objects. Could be a time-shift during DST change or a producer outage. Any KMS errors in logs?
support_alex: customer forwarded a forwarder log snippet: `WARN forwarder: decrypt failed, skipping batch, Key=alias/old-acme-key, reason=AccessDenied`
eng_raj: that smells like a key rotation where the forwarder role lost decrypt on the new key or the alias was repointed. Do we have the forwarder service principal in the new key policy?
support_alex: checking with infra, they confirmed alias was repointed at ~02:05 UTC across accounts (rotation job). SplunkBot: "sec_bot: KMS key rotation: alias/redwood-export-acme was updated by infra-bot at 2026-03-15T02:04:12Z"
sre_maya: if decrypt failed the forwarder would drop the batch (we have that behavior to avoid exposing partial data). That would create a hole unless replay/backfill runs. Did the replay job run?
support_alex: customer says replay didn't run automatically; they see zero-byte manifests for that hour. Example command they used to repro: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/exports?tenant=acme&start=2026-03-15T02:00:00Z&end=2026-03-15T03:00:00Z"` -> response: `{"files": []}`
eng_raj: ok. Short-term mitigation: re-run reencrypt/replay for that tenant for the window. Longer-term: ensure KMS key policy rotation includes forwarder role and preserve alias during rolling rotation.
support_alex: infra gave the KMS policy diff, forwarder role arn: `arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/redwood-forwarder-acme`. New key policy is missing that principal.
sre_maya: steps I'll put in playbook: 1) re-add forwarder role to new key policy 2) run `aws s3 cp s3://redwood-audit-exports/acme/2026-03-15/02/part-0001.gz /tmp/` — if decrypt fails use `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://part-0001.enc --encryption-context Tenant=acme` to validate. 3) trigger reencrypt job: `POST /internal/forwarder/reencrypt?tenant=acme&start=2026-03-15T02:00:00Z&end=2026-03-15T03:00:00Z`
eng_raj: add one more check: verify object timestamps vs metadata. We had a case where S3 object key used producer-local time (offset) and manifest generation normalized to UTC, causing off-by-one-hour buckets. Run `aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-audit-exports --key acme/2026-03-15/02/part-0001.gz --query "{LastModified: LastModified, Metadata: Metadata}"` to inspect.
support_alex: I ran head-object on the neighbouring file and it shows `LastModified: 2026-03-15T01:58:49Z` and metadata `x-amz-meta-tenant: acme, x-amz-meta-ts: 2026-03-15T01:58:41-07:00` — aha, producer recorded local tz (-07:00) in metadata and our manifest generator normalized to UTC, but the forwarder also used metadata-ts and dropped any batch where decrypt failed regardless of key.
eng_raj: so two issues: key policy rotation + inconsistent timestamp metadata. We need to: A) fix key policy and re-encrypt; B) add toleration for timestamp offset during manifest generation or normalize by parsing timezone offsets.
sre_maya: I'll open an infra ticket to add forwarder role to new key policy and kick the replay. support_alex, please ask customer to hold on until we confirm replay success.
support_alex: told the customer. They asked for ETA — can we give one?
eng_raj: if infra approves policy change now we can re-encrypt and replay within ~60 minutes for that hour window. Noting this is a manual unblock.
support_alex: customer replied: "thanks, please rerun and confirm when logs are in Splunk". solutions_tim: tagging splunk-ops, I'll watch ingestion and confirm once replay finishes. :thumbsup:
sec_bot: automated alert: "replay_job_started tenant=acme window=2026-03-15T02:00:00Z/2026-03-15T03:00:00Z job_id=rp-789"
support_alex: I'll update thread when splunk-ops confirms. Bottom line: root cause = KMS alias rotation removed forwarder role from policy -> decrypt failures -> dropped batches; secondary issue = timezone offsets in producer metadata created bucket/manifest mismatches. Action items assigned.
eng_raj: follow-up: add pre-rotation checklist to ensure forwarding principals are preserved and add a small parser in manifest job to handle tz offsets.
support_alex: noted. Closing loop with customer after verification. :lock:
